The Court made the following order:
The petitioners herein contend that they are the owners of Ac.12.07 cents of land in Sy.Nos.11/1 and 11/2 and Ac.1.92 cents of land in Sy.No.18 of Pulikallu Village,
Podalakur Mandal, Nellore District.

The respondent- authorities had taken advance possession of this land in 1984, on 05.05.1984, for the purposes of creation of an Anuku Subbaiah Died vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28808255/
1 earth bund for the Telugu Ganga Project.
2.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contend that advance possession was taken over with the promise of acquiring the land and paying compensation under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
Subsequently land acquisition proceedings had been initiated in relation to this land as well as the neigbouring lands.

However, the acquisition proceedings did not culminateina notification, under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, as the respondents were not clear as to whether the petitioners were to be treated as pattadars of the land or as assignees.
3. The petitioners had made various representations including representation,dated 25.07.2013, for payment of compensation after completing the proceedings under the Land Acquisition Act.
As no steps were being taken by the respondent-authorities, a legal notice had also been issued on 17.03.2015.

Subsequently, the present Writ Petition came to be filed for a direction to the official respondents to initiate acquisition proceedings under the relevant law and for payment of compensation thereon.
4.

The material placed before this Court and the counter affidavits filed by the official respondents would show that the official respondents were not clear as to the status of the land and the claims of the petitioners over the said land.

After prolonged correspondence between various official respondents, a consensus appears to have been arrived that the land would have to be treated as private patta land, as the petitioners were being treated as pattadars.

This consensus was on the ground that the petitioners were purchasers of the land from the original assignees, who had been assigned land prior to 1954 and that the subsequent sale of land by the original assignees cannot be faulted as there was no condition of non-alienation in any assignment of land prior to 1954.

5. The communication of the Special Collector, Telugu Ganga Project, dated 18.12.2024, to the Executive Engineer, Telugu Ganga Project shows that steps have been taken to acquire the land under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.

The counter affidavit filed by the Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, who is arrayed as respondent No.4, states that the acquisition proceedings would have to be initiatedand that land was already handed over to the Executive Engineer, Telugu Ganga Project, Division No.1, on 05.05.1984 itself.
6. The Engineer-in-Chief, who is arrayed as respondent No.5, has also filed a counter affidavit.

In this counter it is stated that proposals for acquisition of the land in Sy.Nos.11/1 and 11/2 had been submitted by the Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition vide letter RC.B.936/85, dated 28.02.1994, and that the District Collector by a letter, dated 08.10.2014, to the Special Collector had also instructed the Special Collector to takeaction as per the Land Acquisition Act.
Consequent to this instruction, the Special Deputy Collector is said to have called for submission of the original DKT pattas from the petitioners.

7. In the light of these pleadings, it is clear that the official respondents have accepted the fact that the lands would have to be treated as private patta land and that land acquisition proceedings would have to be initiated for payment of compensation.

However, land acquisition proceedings had not been initiated by the Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition on the ground that requisitions Anuku Subbaiah Died vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28808255/
2 have not been received from the Irrigation Department.

entities.text: Anuku Subbaiah Died vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the Irrigation Department has taken the stand that it has already sent its requisition and further requisition is not necessary.

8. The rights of the petitioners, which have remained in limbo for the last 40 years, cannot be the denied merely because certain formalities are not completed between two departments of the government.

Once it is accepted that the land in question is not a government land and is private land for which compensation has to be paid, there cannot be any delay in completing the necessary formalities under the Land Acquisition Act.

In such circumstances, there can only be a direction to the respondents to initiate the land acquisition proceedings within a period of one month from today without any further insistences for any requisition from the Irrigation Department.
9. At this stage, it is also necessary to note that respondents 8 and 9 have now raised a claim of ownership over the very same land.

The question as to who is the owner of the land in question has to be determined in the land acquisition proceedings in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (hereinafter referred to as '2013 Act').
10.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Accordingly, this Writ Petition is allowed directing the respondents 1 to 6 to initiate the land acquisition proceedings in relation to the aforesaid land and appurtenant trees and structures admeasuring Ac.12.07 cents of land in Sy.Nos.11/1 and 11/2 and Ac.1.92 cents of land in Sy.No.18 of Pulikallu Village, Podalakur Mandal, Nellore District, within a period of one month from today

and it is left open to the petitioners and respondents 8 and 9 to settle their issue of title and claim, failing which, the same shall be referred for appropriate adjudication before the appropriate Court, in accordance with the terms of The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.
